To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the glucagon receptor can be expressed in mammalian cell lines, that the expressed receptor binds glucagon, that the receptor can cause an increase in the concentration of intracellular cAMP, and that the receptor can also increase the concentration of intracellualar calcium.

we have cloned the receptor for the peptide hormone, glucagon, that is expressed on the cell surface of kidney cells and that when this receptor is activated, it leads to an increase in the concentration of two intracellular messengers, c AMP and calcium.
we cloned a glucagon receptor and that the glucagon receptor is capable of transducing signals to both cAMP and calcium.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation and characterization of the gene encoding the glucagon receptor and the expression of the receptor protein in several different mammalian cell lines.
the molecular basis of the glucagon receptor and the mechanisms of its action.
understanding the structure of the glucagon receptor and the signaling mechanisms that lead to changes in the concentration of intracellular messengers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the glucagon receptor is the primary target of glucagon in the liver and is responsible for the regulation of blood glucose concentration by glucagon.
glucagon is a peptide hormone that is produced and secreted from pancreatic α cells in response to a variety of stimuli.

the cloned glucagon receptor is the first receptor for a member of the glucagon family of peptide hormones to be cloned and expressed in a cell line and that the cloned glucagons receptor transduces signals leading to the generation of both cAMP and intracellular calcium.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have cloned the receptor for glucagon, a hormone that controls blood glucose concentrations.
the glucagon receptor is a member of a family of G-protein-linked receptors that are coupled to both adenylate cyclase and phospholipase C.

we have isolated and characterized the glucagon receptor and have shown that it is a member of a large family of receptors that transduce signals leading either to an increase in intracellular concentrations of calcium or of cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cyclic AMP).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the glucagon receptor is a G-protein-coupled receptor that can signal through both cAMP- and Ca ^{2+} -mediated pathways.
we identified a receptor that is responsible for the biological effects of the hormone glucagon.
the glucagon receptor is an important regulator of blood glucose concentrations, especially during times when the concentration of glucose in the blood is elevated.
